title: Kollektiv suite manifest
description: The per-repo manifest every suite-kit skill reads before doing anything. Product-specific facts live here, next to the code they constrain, rather than inside the plugin — which is what keeps the plugin's skills generic. A skill that cannot find this file says so and stops rather than guessing; this schema exists so that a file which is found is also trustworthy. See docs/adopting.md.

repoRelativePath.description: A path relative to the repo root. Leading slashes are rejected so that a path is never accidentally absolute on one machine and relative on another.

name.description: Label for the health report table. Short and lowercase — 'typecheck', not 'Run the TypeScript compiler'.

run.description: The command, run through a shell.

cwd.description: Working directory for this command, relative to the repo root. Defaults to the repo root. This is what lets one ordered list mix toolchains living at different depths — Konnekt runs pnpm from frontend/ and go from the root.

healthInvariant.description: A grep that must find nothing. These are the checks a linter cannot express.

grep.description: Regular expression. A match is a candidate, not a finding — the diagnosis says how to judge it.

paths.description: Paths the invariant covers. Required and non-empty: an invariant applied to the wrong paths is worse than no invariant, because it reports clean.

exclude.description: Glob patterns exempted from the search. May be empty, but must be stated deliberately.

expect.description: The only supported expectation today. Present so that a future inverted check is a schema change rather than a silent reinterpretation of existing entries.

diagnosis.description: What a match means, the specific silent failure behind it, and any legitimate exception. Required, and required to be substantial: an invariant without a stated reason gets deleted the first time it is inconvenient, and a reviewer with no diagnosis judges a match against the regex instead of against the rule.

reference.description: The document explaining why this rule exists, to be read before deciding a match is acceptable.

healthGenerated.description: A generator whose output is committed. Re-running it must change nothing.

expectCleanDiff.description: Repo-relative paths that must be unchanged after the generator runs. A non-empty diff means either a generated file was hand-edited or a generator change was committed without its output.

requiresNetwork.description: Whether the generator fetches. When true and the machine is offline, the check is reported as skipped with that reason — never as passing.

healthMemory.description: A repo over the suite's always-loaded memory budget, holding its own ceiling while it comes down. Omitted by every repo that is inside the budget, which is the normal case: the check runs on every repo whether or not this is declared, because a repo pays the context cost either way and a check a repo opts into is a check a new repo silently lacks.

maxLines.description: This repo's current ceiling, in lines of always-loaded memory. A ratchet, like the aislop size limits and the coverage floors: it is seeded at what the repo measures today and only ever lowered. The minimum of 201 is what makes the field temporary rather than a permanent licence — a repo that reaches the suite budget can no longer express this key at all and has to delete it.

reason.description: Why this repo is still over, and what is being done about it. An issue number belongs here.

product.description: Display name, as it should appear in a report.

kind.description: Stack shape. Free-form so a fourth product on an unanticipated stack is not a schema change. Known values: 'wails-desktop', 'vite-web', 'workspace-root'.

linear.description: Present when this repo is tracked in Linear directly, bypassing the GitHub-Issues mirror. Exactly one of 'linear' or 'tracking' must be set — tracking is a per-repo choice, and a repo that declares neither would leave /suite-kit:suite-sync guessing where its issues live.

team.description: Team key, e.g. 'KOL'. A key declared here may not yet be provisioned in the workspace — declaring a key and creating the team are different steps.

tracking.description: Present when this repo's issues live on GitHub, which /suite-kit:suite-sync then mirrors into Linear. Every repo in the suite uses this today — GitHub Issues is the one source of truth for work items across the suite.

roadmap.description: Direction and sequencing only — not a work-item list. Work items live in GitHub Issues; /suite-kit:suite-sync mirrors them into Linear, matching on a 'Source: <owner>/<repo>#<number>' line in each Linear issue's description, never on titles.

tokens.description: Omitted by the workspace root, which authors the token set as raw data rather than styled application code.

role.description: Always 'consumer' in a repo carrying this file. The set is defined in kollektiv's design/tokens.json and nowhere else — a repo that both produced and consumed it is the round trip that makes regeneration unsafe.

source.description: The repo the values come from.

sourceFile.description: The vendored copy of that source, conventionally 'tokens.source.json'. Vendored rather than referenced so a product builds from a standalone clone. Editing it directly is a mistake: the next sync-tokens.sh overwrites it and the other product never sees the value.

generate.description: Command that regenerates this repo's token output from the vendored source.

enforce.description: 'strict' — a literal hex or arbitrary px in the covered paths is a failure. 'migrating' — pre-existing matches are expected and reported, not mass-rewritten, while new code is held to strict.

minecraft.description: Omitted by a repo that emits no Minecraft commands.

targetVersion.description: The version this repo emits for.

dataSource.description: Where pinned registry data comes from, including how it is pinned. Pin by tag, never by branch — a branch makes a reproducible build a moving target.

traitMatrix.description: The version-trait document. Serializers branch on a named trait from this matrix and never compare version strings.

health.description: What this repo's health means. /suite-kit:health runs every entry and does not stop at the first failure.

commands.description: Ordered. An entry that cannot run yet is reported as skipped with a reason, never as passing.

invariants.description: Omitted where the repo has none. Nothing is invented to fill the slot.

generated.description: A repo may have more than one generator.

memory.description: Declared only by a repo over the always-loaded memory budget. See docs/conventions.md § The agent memory budget.
